Short title extent and commencement

THE CONTEMPT OF COURTS ACT, 1926
THE CONTEMPT OF
COURTS ACT, 1926
ACT No. XII OF
1926
(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India,
1925, Pt. V, p. 42, and for Report of Select Committee, see ibid., p. 249.
This Act has been applied to Phulera in the Excluded Area of
Upper Tanawal to the extent the Act is applicable in the N.‑W.F.P., and
also extended to the Excluded Area of Upper Tanawal (N ‑W.F.P.) other
than Phulera with effect from such date and subject to such modifications as
may be notified‑see N: W.F.P. (Upper Tanawal) (Excluded Area) Laws
Regulation, 1950.)
[8th March, 1926]
An Act to define and limit the powers of certain Courts in
punishing contempts of courts.
WHEREAS doubts have arisen as to
the powers of a High Court of Judicature to punish contempts of (The word "subordinate" omitted by the Contempt of
Courts (Amdt.) Act, 1937 (12 of 1937), s. 2.)* Courts ;
AND WHEREAS it is expedient to
resolve these doubts and to define and limit the powers exercisable by High
Courts (The words "and Chief Courts" omitted
by the Contempt of Courts (Amdt.) Ordinance, 1959 (45 of 1959), s. 2 (with
effect from the 13th September, 1959).)* in punishing contempts of court
;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
1. Short title extent and
commencement-----(1) This Act may be called the Contempt of Courts Act,
[(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.](Subs. ibid. s. 3 (with effect from the 13th
September, 1959), for sub‑section (2) as amended by A. O., 1949.)
(3) It shall come into force on
such date (The 1st May, 1926 ; see Gazette of India,
1926, Pt. I, p. 442.) as the (Subs. by A. O.,
1937, for "G. G. in C.".)[Central Government] may, by
notification in the (Subs. ibid., for "Gazette of
India".)[official Gazette], appoint.

(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India,

This Act has been applied to Phulera in the Excluded Area of
Upper Tanawal to the extent the Act is applicable in the N.‑W.F.P., and
also extended to the Excluded Area of Upper Tanawal (N ‑W.F.P.) other
than Phulera with effect from such date and subject to such modifications as

Regulation, 1950.)
[8th March, 1926]
An Act to define and limit the powers of certain Courts in
punishing contempts of courts.
WHEREAS doubts have arisen as to
the powers of a High Court of Judicature to punish contempts of (The word "subordinate" omitted by the Contempt of
Courts (Amdt.) Act, 1937 (12 of 1937), s. 2.)* Courts ;
AND WHEREAS it is expedient to
resolve these doubts and to define and limit the powers exercisable by High
Courts (The words "and Chief Courts" omitted
by the Contempt of Courts (Amdt.) Ordinance, 1959 (45 of 1959), s. 2 (with
effect from the 13th September, 1959).)* in punishing contempts of court
;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
2. Power of superior courts to
punish contempts of court--‑(1) Subject to the provisions of sub‑section
(3), the High Courts (The words "of Judicature
established by Letters Patent" omitted by Ordinance 45 of 1959, s. 4 (with
effect from the 13th September, 1959).)* * * shall have and exercise the
same jurisdiction, powers and authority, in accordance with the same procedure
and practice, in respect of contempts of courts subordinate to them as they
have and exercise in respect of contempts of them selves.
* * * * * * * * * *( Sub‑section (2) as amended by the Contempt of Courts
(Capital of the Federation) Order, 1953 (G. G. O. 1 of 1953), omitted by
Ordinance 45 of 1959, s. 4 (with effect from the 13th September, 1959).)
(3) No High (This sub‑section and section 3 have been amended in
their applica tion to the Province of Sind by the Contempt of Courts Sind
(Amdt.) Act, 1951 (2 of 1951), ss. 2 and 3.)Court (The words "or Chief Court", which were ins. by G.
G. O. 1 of 1953, omitted by Ordinance 45 of 1959, s. 4 (with effect from the
13th September, 1959).)* * * shall take cognisance of a con tempt
alleged to have been committed in respect of a Court sub ordinate to it where
such contempt is an offence punishable under the Pakistan Penal Code.
sections.punishment: punishable under the Pakistan Penal Code.

Limit of punishment for contempts of court

THE CONTEMPT OF COURTS ACT, 1926
THE CONTEMPT OF
COURTS ACT, 1926
ACT No. XII OF
1926
(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India,
1925, Pt. V, p. 42, and for Report of Select Committee, see ibid., p. 249.
This Act has been applied to Phulera in the Excluded Area of
Upper Tanawal to the extent the Act is applicable in the N.‑W.F.P., and
also extended to the Excluded Area of Upper Tanawal (N ‑W.F.P.) other
than Phulera with effect from such date and subject to such modifications as
may be notified‑see N: W.F.P. (Upper Tanawal) (Excluded Area) Laws
Regulation, 1950.)
[8th March, 1926]
An Act to define and limit the powers of certain Courts in
punishing contempts of courts.
WHEREAS doubts have arisen as to
the powers of a High Court of Judicature to punish contempts of (The word "subordinate" omitted by the Contempt of
Courts (Amdt.) Act, 1937 (12 of 1937), s. 2.)* Courts ;
AND WHEREAS it is expedient to
resolve these doubts and to define and limit the powers exercisable by High
Courts (The words "and Chief Courts" omitted
by the Contempt of Courts (Amdt.) Ordinance, 1959 (45 of 1959), s. 2 (with
effect from the 13th September, 1959).)* in punishing contempts of court
;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
3. Limit of punishment for
contempts of court.---( This sub‑section and
section 3 have been amended in their applica tion to the Province of Sind by
the Contempt of Courts Sind (Amdt.) Act, 1951 (2 of 1951), ss. 2 and 3.)Save
as otherwise expressly provided by any law for the time being in force, a
contempt of court may be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may
extend to six months, or with fine, which may extend to two thousand rupees, or
with both:
Provided that the accused may be
discharged or the punishment awarded may be remitted on apology being made to
the satisfaction of the Court:
[Provided further that
notwithstanding anything (Provisions ins the Contempts
of Courts (Amdt) Act, 1937 (12 of 1937) s,3) elsewhere contained in any
law no High Court (The words or Chief Court which were ins by the)* * * shall
impose a sentence in excess of that specified in this section for any contempt
either in respect of itself or of a Court subordinate to it.]
